# Tackle Design System

Source: `@tackle-io/design-system` ([GitHub](https://github.com/tackle-io/design-system))

## Setup Gate (MANDATORY — run before writing any code)

Before generating any UI, verify the design system is available in the current project:

### 1. Check for the package

Look for `@tackle-io/design-system` in `package.json` `dependencies` or `devDependencies`.

If **missing**, install it:

```bash
npm install @tackle-io/design-system
```

If the project has no `package.json` yet, initialize one first (`npm init -y`), then install.

### 2. Verify component exports

After confirming the package is installed, read the package entry point to confirm the components and tokens referenced in this skill are real and importable:

```bash
# Quick check — should list all exported component and token names
node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('@tackle-io/design-system')))"
```

If the above fails (e.g. ESM-only), open `node_modules/@tackle-io/design-system/dist/index.js` or the package's `exports` field in its `package.json` and confirm the shell components (`ApplicationShell`, `SalesforceOpportunityShell`, `SalesforceDrilldownShell`) are exported.

### 3. Ensure styles are loaded

Check that the app's root entry point (e.g. `main.tsx`, `index.tsx`, or `App.tsx`) includes:

```ts
import '@tackle-io/design-system/styles';
```

If missing, add it as the **first** import in the entry file so CSS variables and component styles are available globally.

`@tackle-io/design-system/styles` resolves to the **built** `dist/index.css`, which bundles both design tokens (CSS variables) and all component styles. The design-system package must be built (`npm run build`) before publishing or packing.

### 4. Reference the source when in doubt

If you need to verify a component's props, variants, or behavior beyond what this skill documents, read the source directly:

- **Local:** `node_modules/@tackle-io/design-system/src/components/{ComponentName}/`
- **GitHub:** `https://github.com/tackle-io/design-system/tree/main/src/components/{ComponentName}/`

NEVER guess at component APIs. If a component or prop is not documented in this skill or its [component-reference.md](component-reference.md), check the source before using it.

---

## Foundation Gate (MANDATORY — do not skip)

**Every Tackle page, screen, or prototype MUST use one of the approved shell components as its outermost layout wrapper.** There are no exceptions. Never build a custom sidebar, navigation panel, or page shell.

Before writing any UI code, determine the product context and select the correct shell:

| Context                                         | Shell component                     | When to use                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Tackle Platform**                             | `ApplicationShell`                  | Standalone Tackle Platform pages. Provides the Navigation sidebar + main content area.                                                                                                                                             |
| **Tackle for Salesforce — Opportunity record**  | `SalesforceOpportunityShell`        | The Salesforce Opportunity Record page with the Tackle Card in the sidebar.                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Tackle for Salesforce — Detail or form page** | `SalesforceDrilldownShell`          | Tackle Platform detail drill-down and form pages rendered in Salesforce through a canvas iFrame. These are Platform pages hosted inside Salesforce — they use Platform content patterns but render without the Navigation sidebar. |
| **Tackle in AppDirect**                         | `ApplicationShell` (future variant) | Embedded in AppDirect. ADDS for top bar + left nav; Tackle for main content.                                                                                                                                                       |

If the product context is ambiguous, **stop and ask** before proceeding.

NEVER:

- Build a custom sidebar, nav panel, or page layout from scratch
- Use raw `Navigation`, `NavHeader`, `NavMenuItem`, or `NavFooter` to assemble your own shell
- Render page content outside of an approved shell component
- Use `ApplicationShell` when the page will be rendered inside Salesforce canvas
- Use `SalesforceOpportunityShell` for anything other than the Salesforce Opportunity Record page
- Create custom React components for UI elements that exist in `@tackle-io/design-system` (buttons, alerts, modals, form controls, tags, tooltips, menus, tabs, etc.) — always use the design system component
- Use hardcoded colors, spacing, typography, or elevation values — always use design tokens

## Imports

```tsx
// Components + tokens from the single package
import { Button, Alert, Modal, theme } from '@tackle-io/design-system';
import type { ButtonProps, ModalAction } from '@tackle-io/design-system';
```

```css
/* Tokens + component styles — load once at app root */
@import '@tackle-io/design-system/styles';
```

```ts
// JS token objects (for runtime / theme bridging)
import {
  theme,
  colorValues,
  spacingValues
} from '@tackle-io/design-system/tokens';
```

## Component Inventory

Use **only** these exported components. Never create a custom version when one exists.

### Layout & Shell

`ApplicationShell`, `SalesforceOpportunityShell`, `SalesforceDrilldownShell`, `SkipLink`, `PageTitle`, `Navigation`, `NavHeader`, `NavMenuItem`, `NavFooter`

### Forms & Inputs

`Button`, `TextField`, `Checkbox`, `CheckboxGroup`, `Radio`, `RadioGroup`, `Switch`, `SwitchGroup`, `ComboBox`, `Dropdown`, `FormLabel`, `HelperText`, `GroupLabel`, `SelectionTag`

### Feedback & Messaging

`Alert`, `Banner`, `Tooltip`, `Modal`, `ModalHeader`

### Navigation & Data

`Tabs`, `Menu`, `MenuListItem`, `Tag`, `TackleCard`

For the complete props API of each component, see [component-reference.md](component-reference.md).

## Icons

Import named icons directly. All accept `size` (`small`|`medium`|`large`|`xl` or number) and default to `currentColor`.

```tsx
import { SearchIcon, AddIcon, CoSellIcon } from '@tackle-io/design-system';
<SearchIcon size="medium" />;
```

Categories: **Tackle Domain** (AWS, Azure, CoSell, Offers, etc.), **Symbols** (Calendar*, User*, Money, etc.), **Warning & Info** (Check, Error, Help, Info, Warning), **Actions** (Add, Arrow*, Caret*, Close, Copy, Delete, Edit, Search, Sort\*, etc.), **Form** (CheckboxOn/Off/Indeterminate, RadioOn/Off).

Full icon list in [component-reference.md](component-reference.md).

## Token System

Tokens are the **only** approved source for color, spacing, typography, elevation, and layout values.

### CSS Variables (preferred in stylesheets)

| Domain         | Pattern                       | Examples                                                                           |
| -------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Color          | `var(--color-{scale}-{step})` | `--color-blue-40`, `--color-neutral-100`                                           |
| Semantic color | `var(--color-{role})`         | `--color-primary`, `--color-error`, `--color-text-primary`, `--color-bg-secondary` |
| Spacing        | `var(--spacing-{size})`       | `--spacing-xs` (8px) through `--spacing-xl` (64px)                                 |
| Typography     | `var(--font-size-{name})`     | `--font-size-body` (16px), `--font-weight-semibold` (600)                          |
| Elevation      | `var(--elevation-{level})`    | `--elevation-100` through `--elevation-500R`                                       |
| Layout         | `var(--layout-{area})`        | `--layout-header-global` (64px), `--layout-panel-left` (240px)                     |
| Focus          | `var(--focus-ring-{prop})`    | `--focus-ring-color`, `--focus-ring-width` (2px)                                   |
| Border radius  | `var(--border-radius-base)`   | 8px                                                                                |

### JS Token Objects (for runtime / theme bridging)

```ts
theme.colors.primary; // '#2684FF'
theme.spacing.md; // '24px'
theme.typography.fontSize.body; // '16px'
theme.elevation[200]; // box-shadow string
theme.borderRadius.base; // '8px'
```

Full token values in [token-reference.md](token-reference.md).

## Styling Rules

1. **CSS variables** for all visual values — never hardcode hex, px spacing, or font stacks.
2. **Styling approach** matches the codebase: CSS Modules (`.module.css`) or plain CSS with `tackle-` prefixed BEM classes. No Tailwind, no styled-components inside the design system.
3. **Semantic color tokens first** (`--color-primary`, `--color-text-secondary`) before reaching for scale tokens (`--color-blue-40`).
4. **Focus states** use `--focus-ring-color`, `--focus-ring-width`, `--focus-ring-offset`.
5. **Elevation** maps to intent: `100` = resting card, `200` = hover/menu, `300` = selected, `400` = modal/overlay, `500L`/`500R` = directional panels.
6. **Border radius** is always `var(--border-radius-base)` (8px) unless a component explicitly overrides.
7. **Font family** is always `var(--font-family-primary)` — never set a custom font stack.

## Accessibility

The design system components handle their own internal a11y (focus traps, semantics, ARIA). Composition-level concerns (form structure, label association across fields, focus management between views, page landmarks, heading hierarchy) and any custom UI you write are not covered by the components — load the [tackle-accessibility](../tackle-accessibility/SKILL.md) skill whenever you build, modify, or compose UI.

Quick reference for design-system specifics:

- WCAG 2.2 AA compliance is required.
- Components use `@base-ui/react` for keyboard, focus management, and ARIA primitives.
- `SkipLink` must wrap the shell: `<SkipLink /><ApplicationShell ...>`.
- `Alert` defaults: `role="alert"` for `error`/`warning`, `role="status"` for `success`/`info`.
- `CheckboxGroup`/`RadioGroup`/`SwitchGroup` render as `<fieldset>` + `<legend>`.
- `iconOnly` buttons require `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Screen-reader utility class: `.sr-only`.
- Tests use `vitest-axe` / `axe-core` for automated a11y checks.

## Composition Patterns

### Page skeleton

```tsx
<SkipLink />
<ApplicationShell
  logo={<TackleFavIcon />}
  navigationItems={items}
  activeNavigationItemId="cosell"
  accountName="Acme Corp"
  environmentLabel="Production"
  userName="Jane Doe"
  userEmail="jane@acme.com"
>
  <PageTitle
    title="Co-Sell Opportunities"
    primaryAction={{ label: 'Create', onClick: handleCreate }}
  />
  {/* Main content */}
</ApplicationShell>
```

### Salesforce Opportunity skeleton

```tsx
<SalesforceOpportunityShell
  opportunityName="Acme Corp — Expansion"
  highlights={[
    { label: 'Amount', value: '$120,000' },
    { label: 'Close Date', value: 'Jun 30, 2026' },
    { label: 'Stage', value: 'Negotiation' }
  ]}
  pathStages={[
    { label: 'Qualification', state: 'done' },
    { label: 'Needs Analysis', state: 'done' },
    { label: 'Negotiation', state: 'active' },
    { label: 'Closed Won', state: 'upcoming' }
  ]}
  tabs={[
    { id: 'details', label: 'Details' },
    { id: 'activity', label: 'Activity' }
  ]}
  activeTab="details"
  onTabChange={setActiveTab}
  sidebarContent={<TackleCard />}
>
  {/* Tab content */}
</SalesforceOpportunityShell>
```

### Salesforce detail / form page skeleton

```tsx
<SalesforceDrilldownShell
  pageTitle="Create Co-Sell Opportunity"
  breadcrumbs={[
    { label: 'Opportunities', onClick: handleBack },
    { label: 'Create Co-Sell Opportunity' }
  ]}
  quickLinks={[
    { label: 'Opportunity details', href: '#details', active: true },
    { label: 'Cloud partner', href: '#partner' },
    { label: 'Review', href: '#review' }
  ]}
  actions={
    <>
      <Button variant="secondary" onClick={handleCancel}>
        Cancel
      </Button>
      <Button variant="primary" onClick={handleSubmit}>
        Submit
      </Button>
    </>
  }
>
  {/* Form content */}
</SalesforceDrilldownShell>
```

### Modal pattern

```tsx
<Modal
  open={open}
  onClose={handleClose}
  title="Confirm action"
  description="This cannot be undone."
  size="small"
  iconType="error"
  primaryAction={{
    label: 'Delete',
    onClick: handleDelete,
    variant: 'destructive'
  }}
  secondaryAction={{ label: 'Cancel', onClick: handleClose }}
/>
```

### Form group pattern

```tsx
<CheckboxGroup
  label="Cloud providers"
  helperText="Select all that apply"
  direction="vertical"
>
  <Checkbox label="AWS" value="aws" />
  <Checkbox label="Azure" value="azure" />
  <Checkbox label="GCP" value="gcp" />
</CheckboxGroup>
```

## Validation Checklist

Before returning any UI code or design, verify:

- [ ] Setup Gate passed — `@tackle-io/design-system` is installed and styles are imported
- [ ] Foundation Gate passed — correct product context determined
- [ ] Only exported components used (no custom duplicates)
- [ ] All colors, spacing, typography, elevation from tokens (no hardcoded values)
- [ ] Semantic tokens preferred over scale tokens
- [ ] Accessibility: ARIA attrs, keyboard nav, focus rings, skip link — load [tackle-accessibility](../tackle-accessibility/SKILL.md) for composition-level a11y
- [ ] Icons imported by name from `@tackle-io/design-system`
- [ ] CSS follows project convention (CSS Modules or `tackle-` BEM)
- [ ] **Correct shell is the outermost wrapper** — `ApplicationShell` for standalone Platform pages, `SalesforceOpportunityShell` for the SF Opportunity Record, `SalesforceDrilldownShell` for Platform detail/form pages rendered in Salesforce canvas
- [ ] UI copy follows Tackle content style (voice, terms, casing, punctuation)
- [ ] Tackle for Salesforce: no fixed positioning, respects Lightning container
